STEP 1 - Scene: A single slice of pizza (red sauce and melted cheese, likely a thin rectangular/New York-style slice) on a large white square plate. Photographed from above, nearly top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white plate is roughly square-ish with a width of about 26 cm (dinner plate). Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm² for a round equivalent; the plate's flat-on width is about 26 cm, so I use ~530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One pizza slice (cheese, tomato sauce, crust).

STEP 4 - Area: The slice is about 12 cm long and 7 cm wide at its widest, roughly a trapezoid of ~65 cm² (a bit less given tapering). That is about 12% of the plate area. Food covers about 12% in total.

STEP 5 - Volume: Slice is about 1.8 cm thick at the crust, thinner at the tip; average height ~1.5 cm. Volume ≈ 65 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 98 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Pizza slice is dense, bread-like with cheese: bulk density ~0.9 g/ml. 98 ml x 0.9 ≈ 88 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cheese pizza with sauce is roughly 260-270 kcal per 100 g (cooked). Use 265 kcal/100 g. 88 g x 2.65 ≈ 233 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single thin-to-medium slice of cheese pizza weighs roughly 80-110 g and has about 230-300 kcal, so the estimate is plausible for what is visible. The plate is otherwise empty, so no other food is counted.

Total: about 88 g, about 233 kcal.
